report.sampleFormatNote: Authentic Citrix NetScaler syslog SSL log lines with standard fields (SPCBId, ClientIP, CipherSuite, etc.) — format looks genuine

findings.issue: Timestamp is wrong. The log timestamp is 10/03/2025:15:38:40 GMT which is Unix epoch 1743691120. The output shows 1759505920 (_time) and 1759505920000 (time), which is approximately September 2025 — off by ~185 days. The date parser appears to have swapped day and month (03 Oct vs 10 Mar) or applied wrong year logic.

tls.certificate is an empty object {} for SSL_HANDSHAKE_SUCCESS client-side events. No certificate data exists in those raw events so the empty object is acceptable structurally, but OCSF expects the tls object to not include certificate if there is nothing to populate. Minor structural noise but not a true data loss.

Event 3 has no TLS version, cipher, or network endpoint IPs because the raw log only carries SubjectName, but the subject string has a leading space that should be trimmed. Also, protocol_name is set to TCP instead of TLS for an SSL log event.
findings.example: "protocol_name": "TCP" on an SSLLOG event; subject: " DC=com,..."

findings.issue: SubjectName and IssuerName values are mapped with a leading space character not present in the original intent, e.g. ' DC=com,DC=afos...' instead of 'DC=com,DC=afos...'.

OCSF expects certificate validity timestamps as Unix epoch integers (Long type) in the fingerprints/certificate object. The pipeline maps them as raw strings 'Feb 12 21:07:48 2025 GMT' instead of converting to epoch milliseconds.

protocol_name is set to 'TLS' but OCSF Network Activity expects an IANA transport protocol (TCP/UDP). TLS is an application-layer protocol; the correct value should be 'TCP' with TLS details in the tls object. However, setting TCP on event 3 (SUBJECTNAME) while TLS on events 1/2 is internally inconsistent.
findings.example: "protocol_name": "TLS" vs OCSF expects IANA transport layer e.g. TCP

findings.issue: Event 4 (Backend SSL_HANDSHAKE_SUCCESS) contains 'SERVER_AUTHENTICATED' flag in the raw log, which is a meaningful security attribute but was not mapped to any OCSF field (e.g., tls.server_authenticated or unmapped).
findings.example: Raw: '- SERVER_AUTHENTICATED -' — not present in output

findings.issue: log_provider is redundantly set to 'SSLLOG' which is the log subcategory, not a provider. The provider should be 'Citrix' or 'Citrix NetScaler'. OCSF metadata.log_provider is meant for the logging infrastructure name.

category_uid 4 maps to 'Network Activity' in OCSF, but the correct OCSF category name for uid 4 is 'Network Activity' — this is correct. However class_uid 4001 is 'Network Activity' but these are TLS/SSL handshake events which could more precisely map to class 4023 (TLS Activity) in OCSF 1.9. This is a classification choice issue rather than a hard error.
findings.example: class_uid: 4001 used for TLS handshake; OCSF 1.9 defines 4023 for TLS Activity

missingFields: tls.server_authenticated (flag present in raw event 4: SERVER_AUTHENTICATED)
tls.certificate.issuer (IssuerName from event 5 raw log: DC=com,DC=afos,DC=ds,CN=QQ-PKI-INT1 — partial output cut off but the field mapping quality is uncertain)
report.summary: The pipeline correctly identifies the OCSF Network Activity class, extracts most TLS fields (version, cipher, IPs, ports, certificate serial/signature), and preserves unmapped metadata well. However, the timestamp is materially wrong (off by ~185 days, likely a month/day swap in parsing), TLS certificate timestamps are left as raw strings instead of epoch integers, 'SERVER_AUTHENTICATED' is silently dropped, and there is inconsistent use of protocol_name (TLS vs TCP) across event types. These issues — especially the timestamp error — significantly reduce data reliability.
lessons: Always validate parsed timestamps against the source string by spot-checking: NetScaler uses MM/DD/YYYY format, not DD/MM/YYYY — parse order must be enforced explicitly to avoid day/month swaps.

OCSF certificate.created_time and certificate.expiration_time must be Unix epoch Long (milliseconds); always convert 'Mon DD HH:MM:SS YYYY TZ' strings to epoch in the pipeline rather than passing raw strings.

For SSL/TLS log sources, use OCSF class 4023 (TLS Activity) when available in the target schema version instead of the generic 4001 Network Activity; and set connection_info.protocol_name to the IANA transport layer (TCP) not the application protocol (TLS).

Boolean or flag tokens in raw logs (e.g., SERVER_AUTHENTICATED) must be explicitly mapped — either to a defined OCSF boolean field or preserved in unmapped; silent drops cause loss of security-relevant information.
Trim leading/trailing whitespace from parsed field values before mapping; NetScaler SubjectName and IssuerName fields frequently include a leading space after the delimiter.

findings.issue: Client IP address (the querying client) is present in every raw event but is never mapped to any OCSF field. OCSF DNS Activity (4003) requires src_endpoint.ip for the client. E.g. '192.168.1.105' from event 1 is completely absent from the output.
Client source port (e.g. 54321) is present in every raw event but is never mapped. OCSF src_endpoint.port should carry this value.
The resolver/server IP in parentheses at the end of each line (e.g. '192.168.1.1') is present in every raw event but is completely unmapped.
findings.example: (192.168.1.1) → no dst_endpoint.ip or equivalent in output

findings.issue: IPv6 event (2001:db8::1) fails to parse: query.hostname, query.type, query.class, dns.hostname, dns.type, dns.class, dns.flags are all missing/empty. The raw data 'ipv6host.corp.local IN AAAA +' is fully present but not extracted.
findings.example: query: ipv6host.corp.local IN AAAA + → output query:{}, dns:{rcode:'NOERROR'}

findings.issue: IPv6 client address 2001:db8::1 is not mapped, same gap as IPv4 but additionally the entire event parsing fails.
metadata.logged_time is populated with the PID (12345/12346) from the named[] field instead of the actual log timestamp. This is a mis-mapping of a numeric field.
findings.example: named[12345] → logged_time: 12345 (should be epoch of Oct 15 08:23:14)

findings.issue: The syslog timestamp has no year; the pipeline injects __ref_year=2025 and computes _time as ~1760516594 (year ~2025-10). Oct 15 2025 epoch is ~1760516594 — this appears plausible, but the __ref_year field is an internal artifact left in the output event rather than stripped, and the computed year should be verified. If the environment is 2024, all timestamps are off by ~1 year.
The syslog source hostname (infoblox-01, infoblox-02) is present in every raw event and should map to observer.hostname or metadata.product.host, but it is never captured.
findings.example: infoblox-01 named[12345] → no observer or device.hostname in output

findings.issue: Query for 'badmalware.evil.ru' is treated as severity_id:1 (Informational/Low). While threat classification requires external enrichment, no indication of elevated severity is applied even for clearly suspicious domains. This is an analysis gap though arguably not a parse defect.
Internal pipeline working field __ref_year is left in the output event, polluting the OCSF payload.
OCSF recommends preserving the original raw log in unmapped.data or raw_data. The original syslog line is entirely absent from output.
findings.example: No raw_data or unmapped field present

findings.issue: OCSF 4003 DNS Activity uses a top-level 'query' object with 'hostname' and 'type' — the pipeline duplicates this into both 'query' and 'dns' sub-objects with identical data, which is redundant and non-standard. The canonical OCSF field is dns.query.

category_uid should be 4 for 'Network Activity' but OCSF DNS Activity class 4003 belongs to category 4003's parent — this is correct. However 'category_uid:4' maps to 'Network Activity' which is correct for DNS. No error but worth confirming.

missingFields: src_endpoint.ip (client IP present in all 8 events, never mapped)
src_endpoint.port (client port present in all 8 events, never mapped)
dst_endpoint.ip (resolver IP in parentheses present in all 8 events, never mapped)
observer.hostname / metadata.product.host (syslog source hostname infoblox-01/02 present in all events, never mapped)
report.summary: The pipeline correctly identifies OCSF class 4003 DNS Activity, extracts the queried hostname/type/class/flags, and handles the NXDOMAIN case with correct rcode/status/activity_id mapping. However it critically drops the client IP, client port, and resolver IP that are present in every single event — these are the most important network-layer fields for DNS activity analysis. The IPv6 client event (event 8) fails to parse entirely, and metadata.logged_time is mis-populated with the process PID rather than the log timestamp. With ~4 high-severity source values unmapped across all 8 events plus a full parse failure on event 8, the pipeline captures only a fraction of what the source provides.
lessons: Always extract and map both sides of the 'client IP#port' pattern in Infoblox DNS logs to OCSF src_endpoint.ip and src_endpoint.port — this is the most critical network field in DNS activity logs.

The resolver IP in parentheses at line end (e.g. '(192.168.1.1)') must be mapped to dst_endpoint.ip or an equivalent OCSF server/observer field; ensure the regex covers both IPv4 and IPv6 parenthetical addresses.
IPv6 addresses in the client field (e.g. '2001:db8::1#53210') require a separate regex branch or a combined pattern — never assume IPv4-only for Infoblox logs.

metadata.logged_time must be set to the parsed event timestamp (epoch ms), not to the process PID extracted from the named[] bracket; separate the PID capture (process.pid) from the timestamp capture.

Strip internal pipeline working fields (e.g. __ref_year) before emitting the final OCSF event, and avoid duplicating data between a top-level 'query' object and a 'dns' sub-object — pick one canonical OCSF location.
Always capture the syslog source hostname (infoblox-01/02) into observer.hostname or metadata.product.host to preserve the originating device identity.

report.sampleFormatNote: Authentic CrowdStrike Falcon event stream with realistic DetectionSummaryEvent, AuthActivityAuditEvent, UserActivityAuditEvent, and IncidentSummaryEvent structures including proper detection IDs, MITRE technique references, and host/process telemetry.

findings.issue: Process information (name, pid, command_line, sha256, sha1, md5, parent_process, parent_pid) is entirely absent from Detection Finding outputs — OCSF requires process object under 'process' for Detection Finding class. All process fields from input are dropped.
findings.example: Input has process.name=powershell.exe, pid=4821, command_line with encoded payload — none appear in output event 1

findings.issue: attacks array is always empty [] despite MITRE technique, technique_name, and tactic being present in every DetectionSummaryEvent. OCSF Detection Finding expects attacks[].technique.uid (e.g. T1059.001), attacks[].technique.name, and attacks[].tactic.name.
file_path is present in every DetectionSummaryEvent but no 'file' object is mapped in output. OCSF Detection Finding supports a file object; this value is silently dropped.

finding.status_id=2 is mapped for 'in_progress' but OCSF Detection Finding status enums are: 0=Unknown,1=New,2=In Progress,3=Suppressed,4=Resolved. 'true_positive' (event 7) has no valid OCSF status_id and is not mapped at all — the field would need unmapped handling or a custom extension declared.
findings.example: Event 7 status='true_positive' — no status_id or status in finding object visible in output snippet

findings.issue: Detection event 3 (DLL injection) has no network block in source, yet src_endpoint and dst_endpoint are output as empty objects {}. OCSF expects these fields to be omitted or null when no data exists, not empty objects.

UserActivityAuditEvent for a policy_update action is mapped to class_uid=3005 (User Access Management). A policy configuration change is better represented by class_uid=3006 (Group Management) or more accurately class_uid=6003 (Config Change / OCSF). Using 3005 misrepresents the semantic of a prevention_policy update.

metadata.uid is set to cid ('a1b2c3d4e5f6789012345678') for auth and user activity events that have no dedicated event ID. This makes uid non-unique across events of the same cid. A derived unique ID (e.g. cid+timestamp+user) should be constructed.
external_ip is present in all DetectionSummaryEvent host_info blocks but is not mapped into the device object or any OCSF endpoint field.
findings.example: Input: host_info.external_ip='203.45.167.89' — absent from output device object

findings.issue: IncidentSummaryEvent (event 6 in input) output is not shown in the 8 pipeline output events, suggesting it may be dropped or the pipeline truncated. If dropped, incident data including fine_score=95.4, hosts list, detection_ids, users_involved, start_time are all lost.
findings.example: Input event 6 is IncidentSummaryEvent with incident_id='inc:a1b2c3d4e5f67890:400001' — not present in output

findings.issue: traffic object is always empty {} in all events. While many events lack byte/packet counts, this field should be omitted rather than emitted as an empty object, and where present (network block exists) basic fields should be populated.

direction_id=0 (Unknown) is hardcoded for all events including those with clear outbound connections (src internal IP → dst external IP). Should be direction_id=2 (Outbound) for events with internal src and external dst.
findings.example: Event 1: src_ip=10.10.4.22 → dst_ip=185.220.101.47 port 443, yet direction_id=0

findings.issue: src_endpoint.port is set to 0 for event 1 rather than being omitted. Source port is not known from the input; emitting 0 is misleading.

severity_id=3 (Medium) is assigned to auth failure events but CrowdStrike AuthActivityAuditEvents carry no severity field — pipeline is inferring/defaulting Medium which is undocumented behavior. Should be severity_id=0 (Unknown) or omitted.
findings.example: Input event 2 has no severity field → output severity_id=3, severity='Medium'

findings.issue: finding.desc duplicates finding.title (both set to detection_name). The desc field should carry a human-readable description. Source doesn't provide a separate description, so this is acceptable but suboptimal.

In OCSF, user objects do not have an 'ip' field. The user_ip for auth events should be mapped to src_endpoint.ip, not actor.user.ip. It is correctly also in src_endpoint but the invalid actor.user.ip field should be removed.
findings.example: output event 2: actor.user.ip='192.168.1.55' — not a valid OCSF user field

findings.issue: OCSF os.type_id for Windows is 100 which is correct, but all non-Windows events (auth audit) emit type_id=0 (Unknown) with no os.name even when the service context implies a known platform. Minor but creates noise.
findings.example: output event 2: device.os:{type_id:0, type:'Unknown'} — no platform context from source

process.sha256 / process.sha1 / process.md5 (file hashes present in source, not mapped to OCSF file.hashes array)

host_info.external_ip (present in all DetectionSummaryEvents, not mapped anywhere)

additional_info.mfa_method / additional_info.browser / additional_info.geo_location (present in auth success event 8, not mapped)

report.summary: The pipeline correctly handles OCSF class routing for DetectionSummaryEvent (2004), AuthActivityAuditEvent (3002), and UserActivityAuditEvent (3005), and timestamps/metadata are well-formed. However, critical content fields present in the source — specifically MITRE attack mappings, process telemetry, file paths, and file hashes — are entirely dropped from output, representing significant information loss for detection-class events. The IncidentSummaryEvent appears to be missing from the output entirely, and structural issues (empty objects, invalid actor.user.ip, wrong direction_id) further reduce fidelity.
lessons: For OCSF Detection Finding (class 2004), always map MITRE technique/tactic from CrowdStrike to attacks[].technique.uid + attacks[].tactic.name — leaving attacks:[] when the source provides T-codes is a critical data loss.

CrowdStrike DetectionSummaryEvent process block must be mapped to OCSF process object with name, pid, cmd_line, and file.hashes (sha256/sha1/md5); parent process maps to process.parent_process; these are the core forensic payload of the event.
Never emit empty objects ({}) for optional OCSF fields like src_endpoint, dst_endpoint, traffic — either populate them or omit entirely to avoid schema pollution.
When source has external_ip separate from local_ip, map external_ip to device.ip_addresses[] or a secondary endpoint field — dropping it loses network context.

metadata.uid must be unique per event; using only cid produces collisions for cid-level events (auth, audit); derive a unique ID by hashing cid+timestamp+action or concatenating available identifiers.

(_evtName == 'CREATE_USER' ? 'User Account Management: Create' : 'User Account Management: Other') : (_evtName == 'download' ? 'File System Activity: Read' : 'File System Activity: Set Attributes'))

add.name: actor
add.value: {'user':{'email_addr':id && actor && actor.email ? actor.email : '','uid':actor && actor.profileId ? actor.profileId : '','name':actor && actor.email ? actor.email : ''}}

functions.description: Map core OCSF fields
Auth-specific fields
Drive file object
Admin user management object
Set _time from OCSF time field

conf.comment: --- STEP 5: Final cleanup — remove raw/intermediate fields ---

functions.description: Remove raw/intermediate source fields

fortinet_fortigate to CommonSecurityLog pipeline.
Parses events, drops noise, maps to CommonSecurityLog schema, and outputs compact JSON.
--- STEP 1: Parse raw events ---

functions.description: Extract CEF extension (if CEF-wrapped)
Set KVP source field
Parse KVP fields
Strip FTNTFGT prefix from FortiGate vendor fields

add.name: dest_ip
add.value: dest_ip || dst_ip || dst || dstaddr || dstip || undefined

add.name: log_time
add.value: eventtime ? Number(String(eventtime).substring(0,13)) : (date && time ? Date.parse(String(date) + 'T' + String(time)) : undefined)

add.name: severity
add.value: level == 'emergency' || level == 'alert' ? 1 : level == 'critical' ? 2 : level == 'error' ? 3 : level == 'warning' ? 4 : level == 'notice' ? 5 : level == 'information' ? 6 : (severity || undefined)

functions.description: Normalize CEF/FortiGate field names to standard

Drop health check / keepalive PING traffic (enable in Cribl UI to activate)

conf.comment: --- STEP 3: Map fields to CommonSecurityLog schema ---
Golden CommonSecurityLog mapping — deterministic from canonical fields (no AI).

functions.description: Set device vendor/product/version

add.name: DeviceVendor
add.value: (vendor) != null && String(vendor) != 'undefined' && String(vendor) != 'null' && String(vendor) != '-' && String(vendor) != '' ? (vendor) : undefined

add.name: DeviceProduct
add.value: (product) != null && String(product) != 'undefined' && String(product) != 'null' && String(product) != '-' && String(product) != '' ? (product) : undefined

add.name: DeviceVersion
add.value: (version) != null && String(version) != 'undefined' && String(version) != 'null' && String(version) != '-' && String(version) != '' ? (version) : undefined

add.name: DeviceEventClassID
add.value: (event_code || asa_code || ftd_code || signature) != null && String(event_code || asa_code || ftd_code || signature) != 'undefined' && String(event_code || asa_code || ftd_code || signature) != 'null' && String(event_code || asa_code || ftd_code || signature) != '-' && String(event_code || asa_code || ftd_code || signature) != '' ? (event_code || asa_code || ftd_code || signature) : undefined

add.name: Activity
add.value: (message || action) != null && String(message || action) != 'undefined' && String(message || action) != 'null' && String(message || action) != '-' && String(message || action) != '' ? (message || action) : undefined

add.name: SourceIP
add.value: (src_ip) != null && String(src_ip) != 'undefined' && String(src_ip) != 'null' && String(src_ip) != '-' && String(src_ip) != '' ? (src_ip) : undefined

add.name: SourcePort
add.value: (src_port) != null && String(src_port) != 'undefined' && String(src_port) != 'null' && String(src_port) != '-' && String(src_port) != '' ? (src_port) : undefined

add.name: DestinationIP
add.value: (dest_ip) != null && String(dest_ip) != 'undefined' && String(dest_ip) != 'null' && String(dest_ip) != '-' && String(dest_ip) != '' ? (dest_ip) : undefined

add.name: DestinationPort
add.value: (dest_port) != null && String(dest_port) != 'undefined' && String(dest_port) != 'null' && String(dest_port) != '-' && String(dest_port) != '' ? (dest_port) : undefined

add.name: Protocol
add.value: (transport || protocol) != null && String(transport || protocol) != 'undefined' && String(transport || protocol) != 'null' && String(transport || protocol) != '-' && String(transport || protocol) != '' ? (transport || protocol) : undefined

add.name: DeviceAction
add.value: (action) != null && String(action) != 'undefined' && String(action) != 'null' && String(action) != '-' && String(action) != '' ? (action) : undefined

add.name: SourceUserName
add.value: (src_user || user) != null && String(src_user || user) != 'undefined' && String(src_user || user) != 'null' && String(src_user || user) != '-' && String(src_user || user) != '' ? (src_user || user) : undefined

add.name: DestinationUserName
add.value: (dest_user) != null && String(dest_user) != 'undefined' && String(dest_user) != 'null' && String(dest_user) != '-' && String(dest_user) != '' ? (dest_user) : undefined

add.name: SentBytes
add.value: (bytes_out) != null && String(bytes_out) != 'undefined' && String(bytes_out) != 'null' && String(bytes_out) != '-' && String(bytes_out) != '' ? (bytes_out) : undefined

add.name: ReceivedBytes
add.value: (bytes_in) != null && String(bytes_in) != 'undefined' && String(bytes_in) != 'null' && String(bytes_in) != '-' && String(bytes_in) != '' ? (bytes_in) : undefined

functions.description: Map canonical fields → Sentinel CommonSecurityLog

add.name: ApplicationProtocol
add.value: (app || protocol) != null && String(app || protocol) != 'undefined' && String(app || protocol) != 'null' && String(app || protocol) != '-' && String(app || protocol) != '' ? (app || protocol) : undefined

add.name: DeviceName
add.value: (host) != null && String(host) != 'undefined' && String(host) != 'null' && String(host) != '-' && String(host) != '' ? (host) : undefined

add.name: LogSeverity
add.value: (severity == null || severity === '' ? 5 : Number(severity) <= 1 ? 10 : Number(severity) == 2 ? 9 : Number(severity) == 3 ? 8 : Number(severity) == 4 ? 6 : Number(severity) == 5 ? 4 : Number(severity) == 6 ? 3 : 1) != null && String(severity == null || severity === '' ? 5 : Number(severity) <= 1 ? 10 : Number(severity) == 2 ? 9 : Number(severity) == 3 ? 8 : Number(severity) == 4 ? 6 : Number(severity) == 5 ? 4 : Number(severity) == 6 ? 3 : 1) != 'undefined' && String(severity == null || severity === '' ? 5 : Number(severity) <= 1 ? 10 : Number(severity) == 2 ? 9 : Number(severity) == 3 ? 8 : Number(severity) == 4 ? 6 : Number(severity) == 5 ? 4 : Number(severity) == 6 ? 3 : 1) != 'null' && String(severity == null || severity === '' ? 5 : Number(severity) <= 1 ? 10 : Number(severity) == 2 ? 9 : Number(severity) == 3 ? 8 : Number(severity) == 4 ? 6 : Number(severity) == 5 ? 4 : Number(severity) == 6 ? 3 : 1) != '-' && String(severity == null || severity === '' ? 5 : Number(severity) <= 1 ? 10 : Number(severity) == 2 ? 9 : Number(severity) == 3 ? 8 : Number(severity) == 4 ? 6 : Number(severity) == 5 ? 4 : Number(severity) == 6 ? 3 : 1) != '' ? (severity == null || severity === '' ? 5 : Number(severity) <= 1 ? 10 : Number(severity) == 2 ? 9 : Number(severity) == 3 ? 8 : Number(severity) == 4 ? 6 : Number(severity) == 5 ? 4 : Number(severity) == 6 ? 3 : 1) : undefined

add.name: RequestURL
add.value: (url) != null && String(url) != 'undefined' && String(url) != 'null' && String(url) != '-' && String(url) != '' ? (url) : undefined

add.name: SourceTranslatedAddress
add.value: (src_translated_ip) != null && String(src_translated_ip) != 'undefined' && String(src_translated_ip) != 'null' && String(src_translated_ip) != '-' && String(src_translated_ip) != '' ? (src_translated_ip) : undefined

add.name: DestinationTranslatedAddress
add.value: (dest_translated_ip) != null && String(dest_translated_ip) != 'undefined' && String(dest_translated_ip) != 'null' && String(dest_translated_ip) != '-' && String(dest_translated_ip) != '' ? (dest_translated_ip) : undefined

sample value "netbios forward" was not extracted/mapped into the output
_time=1783936302.432 does not match the event's eventtime (1757600388.419 ≈ 2025-09-11). The _time appears to be the pipeline processing time, not the log event time

CEF standard mandates use of defined extension key names (src, dst, spt, dpt, proto, act, in, out, deviceExternalId, etc.). Pipeline uses non-standard custom names (src_ip, dest_ip, src_port, dest_port, proto_num, bytes_in, bytes_out) which are not valid CEF extension keys
findings.example: src_ip=10.42.73.127 should be src=10.42.73.127; dest_ip should be dst; spt/dpt instead of src_port/dest_port

findings.issue: policy_name is mapped to the poluuid value instead of policyname. poluuid='0bf82f11-0497-4ded-a4b8-8450c8e9c94a' is placed in policy_name field

src_zone mapping is inconsistent: event 1 uses srcintf value ('REDACTED') while event 2 uses srcintfrole value ('lan'). The logic appears to fall back to srcintfrole when srcintfrole != 'undefined', conflating interface name with zone
Two severity fields with different values exist on the same event: severity=5 and __sev=4. CEF severity should be a single consistent value
FortiGate 'notice' level maps to CEF severity 4 (__sev) or 5 (severity) — CEF uses 0-10 scale. Neither value is documented/consistent, and notice should map to approximately 3-4
version is hardcoded to '7.x' rather than derived from the log; acceptable if source doesn't carry version, but worth noting

report.summary: The pipeline fails to produce actual CEF-formatted output strings. While it correctly parses most FortiGate key=value fields into intermediate JSON and builds a partial CEF header in __hdr, it never assembles the complete CEF event (header + extension) as a formatted _raw string, which is the fundamental requirement of CEF format. Additionally, _time is set to pipeline processing time rather than event time, policy_name is mis-mapped to the poluuid value, CEF standard extension key names are not used, and several source fields (osname, devtype, crscore, unauthuser) are dropped entirely.

add.name: log_time
add.value: log_time || generated_time || receive_time || start_time || event__created || timestamp || event__start

functions.description: Alias Copilot/schematizer OCSF-style fields to canonical names

add.name: _time
add.value: (typeof log_time != 'undefined' && log_time) ? (/^\d{13}$/.test(String(log_time)) ? Number(log_time) : /^\d{10}$/.test(String(log_time)) ? Number(log_time) * 1000 : /^\d{13}\.\d+$/.test(String(log_time)) ? Number(log_time) : /^\d{10}\.\d+$/.test(String(log_time)) ? Number(log_time) * 1000 : new Date(String(log_time)).getTime()) / 1000 : _time

functions.description: Parse AEM access log (NCSA combined format) into structured fields
Normalize protocol, action, and severity based on HTTP status code
Convert numeric string fields to numbers for downstream use

add.name: dest_ip
add.value: dest_ip || dst_ip || destination__ip || server__ip || dstaddr || dstip

add.name: dest_port
add.value: dest_port || dst_port || destination__port || dpt || dstport || dport

add.name: log_time
add.value: log_time || generated_time || receive_time || start_time || event__created || timestamp || event__start

functions.description: Alias Copilot/schematizer OCSF-style fields to canonical names

add.name: _time
add.value: (typeof log_time != 'undefined' && log_time) ? (/^\d{13}$/.test(String(log_time)) ? Number(log_time) : /^\d{10}$/.test(String(log_time)) ? Number(log_time) * 1000 : /^\d{13}\.\d+$/.test(String(log_time)) ? Number(log_time) : /^\d{10}\.\d+$/.test(String(log_time)) ? Number(log_time) * 1000 : new Date(String(log_time)).getTime()) / 1000 : _time

add.name: device

functions.description: Parse ivanti ServiceStatus syslog header: timestamp, host, process, pid, level and message body

Extract service state transition (OLD->NEW) when present

add.name: action

functions.description: Extract fields from admin, security and host checker event messages (admin actions, failed console logins, brute force, host checker failures, malware detection, session hijack)
